properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Homegrown BIP340-Schnorr-style signature implementation over secp256k1 in the walletlib Nostr relay transport (Java counterpart of js src/nostr.ts which uses @noble/curves schnorr). Live, reachable, hand-rolled EC math on BouncyCastle low-level primitives — sign chain at L102-127 (R=G·k, e=hash mod n, s=k+e·d mod n), verify chain at L157-167 (R=s·G−e·P), point decode/create at L386-392. Quantum-unsafe (Shor breaks secp256k1); note also that hand-implemented signature schemes carry their own clas

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in use in the fakewallet BIP39 seed flow (checksum hash over entropy) and in the walletlib Nostr transport (event-ID computation, session identifier derivation, and the tagged-hash helper inside the homegrown Schnorr scheme). SHA-256 is Grover-affected only (square-root speedup); the digest itself is not Shor-broken, but here it feeds the quantum-unsafe secp256k1 signature flows. Changeable here: first-party code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The MWA session cipher is deliberately 128-bit AES: HKDF.hkdfSHA256L16 emits exactly 16 bytes of key material (MobileWalletAdapterSessionCommon:236) wrapped as SecretKeySpec(…, "AES") (:237); the JS side mirrors with { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 128 } (parseHelloRsp.ts:41). Key size is pinned by the MWA protocol specification — observable here, changeable only via a protocol revision. PQ note: Grover halves effective strength to ~64 bits; CNSA 2.0 prefers AES-256.
